feature1.prompt: call_command fails when argument of required mutually exclusive group is passed in kwargs. When executing call_command with a keyword argument (for example, shop_id=1) that belongs to a mutually exclusive group (where either --shop-id or --shop must be provided), a CommandError is raised stating 'Error: one of the arguments --shop-id --shop is required'. This issue occurs because the current implementation only passes options marked as required individually to the parser, ignoring that an option in a mutually exclusive group is effectively required as part of the group. The expected behavior is that providing the argument as a keyword (or as a command-line option) should work without error.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature involves updating the internal logic of the Django management command parser. You need to modify the get_actions function in django/core/management/__init__.py so that when constructing the parse_args list, options that are part of a required mutually exclusive group are properly included. The fix must ensure that even if an individual option is not marked as required, it is recognized as required through its association with a mutually exclusive group.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/core/management/__init__.py; Function: get_actions, specifically in the block where parse_args is constructed. Add logic to iterate over parser._mutually_exclusive_groups and include options from groups where required=True.

feature2.prompt: call_command fails when argument of required mutually exclusive group is passed in kwargs. When using call_command with a keyword argument (such as shop_id=1) that is part of a mutually exclusive group, a CommandError occurs stating that one of the arguments --shop-id --shop is required. The failure indicates that the parser does not recognize that an option within a required mutually exclusive group should be treated as required. The correct behavior is that the command should execute successfully whether the argument is passed as a keyword or as a command-line option.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature focuses on adding new test cases and a test management command to validate the proper handling of mutually exclusive required options. You are to implement a new command in tests/user_commands/management/commands/mutually_exclusive_required.py and update tests in tests/user_commands/tests.py to include a test method that checks the behavior when either of the mutually exclusive options is provided, as well as when neither is provided.
feature2.entrypoint: Files: tests/user_commands/management/commands/mutually_exclusive_required.py (create this new command) and tests/user_commands/tests.py (update to add test_mutually_exclusive_group_required_options). The new test should invoke the command with appropriate parameters to verify that the fix in the core logic works as expected.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with the Django management command system. Feature1 modifies the core logic in django/core/management/__init__.py while feature2 adds tests and a new command that rely on these changes.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 and Feature2 must be integrated so that the updated parsing logic is fully validated by the new test cases. Continuous integration testing should run the full suite to ensure that call_command behaves correctly with mutually exclusive required arguments.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature1 and Feature2 should coordinate on the expected behavior of call_command. Discussions should focus on ensuring that the modifications to the parser correctly support mutually exclusive groups and that the new tests accurately capture the intended functionality.
